editorial-1.firstReading: Adult hugs a toy and recalls childhood comfort.
editorial-1.note: Matching rabbit links present embrace and the remembered scene.

editorial-1.firstReading: Open book reveals a childhood hallway and toy.
editorial-1.note: Domestic hallway visible; the connection to this reader is uncertain.

editorial-1.firstReading: Book evokes an adult-child domestic memory.
editorial-1.note: Open-book trail leads to an adult-child scene.

editorial-1.firstReading: Open book evokes a child and caregiver around a bowl.
editorial-1.note: Book plume and matching bowls link the two spaces.

editorial-1.firstReading: Adult touches a checked cloth with an unclear history.
editorial-1.note: Touch and cloth imply attachment with little evidence of a personal past.

editorial-1.firstReading: Adult slides or retrieves a photo-like card at a slot.
editorial-1.note: The card shows a room whose significance is unclear.

editorial-1.firstReading: Adult hugs a rabbit just removed from a box.
editorial-1.note: Hug conveys attachment without showing the past.

editorial-1.firstReading: Adult looks at rabbit and remembers child with matching toy.
editorial-1.note: Toy repeats in the memory of a child holding it.

editorial-1.firstReading: Open book evokes a childhood kitchen scene.
editorial-1.note: The bowl repeats in the foreground and glowing scene.

editorial-2.firstReading: A woman rests her hand on a worn checked cloth beside a closed book as angled light falls across the table.
editorial-2.note: The cloth and touch suggest an attachment. The light reads as a window pattern and leaves the past uncertain.

editorial-2.firstReading: A woman reads a book that gives rise to a glowing kitchen scene with a child and an older person.
editorial-2.note: The glow links the pages to the domestic scene, with a bowl connecting the scene to the reader's table.

editorial-2.firstReading: A woman lifts a small fish-shaped object from an open case and recalls a child and an older man outdoors by the water.
editorial-2.note: The fish-shaped keepsake appears to be a lure, and the corresponding apparition reads as a shared fishing memory.

editorial-2.firstReading: A woman looks into an open book as a wispy scene of a child and adult at a kitchen table rises above it.
editorial-2.note: The trail from the pages and the bowls in both scenes connect the reading to a domestic memory.

editorial-2.firstReading: A woman holds a stuffed rabbit, with a small photograph on the table that appears to show a child cuddling it.
editorial-2.note: The photograph pairs the present toy with a child holding its likeness. This reads as a personal trace even without an apparition.

editorial-2.firstReading: A woman grips an illustrated card partway out of a counter slot. It shows a room with chairs and a table.
editorial-2.note: The card and slot make the retrieval visually clear. The domestic room's significance to the reader remains uncertain.

editorial-2.firstReading: A woman hugs a stuffed rabbit while a golden image shows a child hugging a similar toy.
editorial-2.note: The toy's long ears and repeated embrace visibly connect the two moments.

editorial-2.firstReading: A woman looks into an open book whose pages form a hallway with a framed picture and a hanging bag.
editorial-2.note: The dimensional hallway makes the book a window into a home. Its connection to the particular reader's past is uncertain.

editorial-2.firstReading: A woman reads beside a patterned bowl while a child and adult gather around another bowl in a floating kitchen scene.
editorial-2.note: The repeating bowl and the visible trail from the book convey a personal kitchen memory.

mascot-1.note: Hands and overlapping paper folds form a visible nook around the button.

mascot-1.firstReading: A dark mitten pinches a ribbon against a gold button at its cuff.
mascot-1.note: The ribbon tip meets the button hole while the other hand braces the button.

mascot-1.firstReading: A ring-bound diary hugs a taped clover card to its cover.

mascot-1.firstReading: A green case cups a gold button against its front.
mascot-1.note: The two inward-facing gloves hold the button close.

mascot-1.firstReading: A mushroom figure supports a gold button dangling from a loop under its cap.
mascot-1.note: A cord suspends the keepsake beneath the cap and the two hands cradle its lower edge.

mascot-1.firstReading: A beret-wearing envelope holds a clover card up toward the viewer.

mascot-1.firstReading: A ribboned green chest clasps a gold button between its padded hands.

mascot-1.firstReading: A clasped green case holds a gold button in both hands.
mascot-1.note: Both hands support the lower edge and keep the button close to the body.

mascot-1.firstReading: A ring-bound scrapbook hugs a clover tag tied with a bow.
mascot-1.note: One arm wraps across and beneath the tag with the other supporting its side.

mascot-2.firstReading: A ring-bound diary holds up a small scalloped paper with a purple flower.
mascot-2.note: The flower angles outward beside the face. The pose reads primarily as showing it.

mascot-2.firstReading: A handled mint case cradles a gold button against its front.
mascot-2.note: Both gloves reach around the lower half of the button to support it.

mascot-2.firstReading: A green box holds a big gold button between its hands at the front of its body.

mascot-2.firstReading: A mushroom figure supports a gold button dangling from a cord under the cap.

mascot-2.firstReading: A pink diary cups a small card with a yellow flower at its center.
mascot-2.note: The flower card is held close and wrapped between two open hands.

mascot-2.firstReading: A diary hugs a square scrap with a purple flower taped to it.

mascot-2.firstReading: A dark mitten manipulates a gold button and a strip of red ribbon at its cuff.

mascot-2.firstReading: An envelope cups a red button tucked inside an open fold.
mascot-2.note: The rounded arms close around the button where the envelope folds shelter it.

mascot-2.firstReading: A handled mint case cradles a gold button between padded gloves.

environment-1.firstReading: An elevated plank walk follows the coast, with short ramps branching toward lower canopy stalls.
environment-1.note: The main walkway is clear. The lower vendor decks could be fixed or floating.

environment-1.firstReading: A shopper follows a boardwalk toward stairs while tall rigs appear to suspend a canopy stall over water.
environment-1.note: The elevated rig and hanging vendor platform plausibly allow vertical repositioning. A route continues along the boardwalk and up the stairs.

environment-1.firstReading: A timber boardwalk reaches toward shore past sloped ramps and low stalls.
environment-1.note: The ramps serve low decks. Flotation or other vertical adaptation is uncertain.

environment-1.firstReading: A vendor area surrounds a narrow boardwalk, with a large hinged-looking timber arm beside the crossing.
environment-1.note: The pivots suggest movable dock hardware, but the connection and tide-related role of the arm remain unclear.

environment-1.firstReading: A raised central walkway connects by short ramps to lower vendor platforms resting close to the water.
environment-1.note: Visible barrel-like supports under the vendor platforms and sloped gangways plausibly allow the stalls to float with the water level.

environment-1.firstReading: An overhead beam and four lines suspend a canopy stall above the water alongside a stepped boardwalk.
environment-1.note: The overhead rig plausibly changes the stall's height while the boardwalk and stairs maintain a public route.

environment-1.firstReading: A cliffside wheel and crane hold a suspended load between the waterline and a market on the stone quay.
environment-1.note: The quay hoist plausibly transfers supplies between changing water height and a fixed vendor level. The stone promenade continues through the stalls.

environment-1.firstReading: A coastal market steps down in terraces toward square decks partly awash by the stone quays.
environment-1.note: Successive landings allow waterfront activity at multiple heights. The upper stairs and promenade remain visibly connected.

environment-1.firstReading: A large wheel and overhead lines hang platforms at different heights beside a busy wooden boardwalk.
environment-1.note: The rig and cage-like suspended deck suggest vendor lifts. The main boardwalk is visibly continuous through the market.

environment-2.firstReading: A long plank walkway branches across sloping gangways to lower stalls beside tall posts with fitted collars.
environment-2.note: The ramps and collars on the guide posts make the low decks readable as platforms that can rise along the posts. The main boardwalk continues past the stalls.

environment-2.firstReading: A raised boardwalk runs toward shore while short hinged-looking ramps connect to market rafts on visible barrels.
environment-2.note: The raft supports meet the water directly, and the sloped ramps connect the floating vendor decks to a continuous walkway.

environment-2.firstReading: A shopper follows a stone quay beside an angled crane that holds a netted box above the water under a stall.
environment-2.note: A visible load and crane make water-to-stall transfer plausible at different water levels. The quay remains a walkable route through the market.

environment-2.firstReading: A timber boardwalk connects by sloped planks to low canopy stalls whose decks meet tall collared posts.
environment-2.note: The collars and low decks make a guided floating arrangement plausible, and the boardwalk leads toward the shore settlement.

environment-2.firstReading: Shoppers cross a planked market walkway beside canopy decks held at different heights on a wall-side pulley structure.
environment-2.note: Raised supports and visible overhead drums give the side decks a plausible way to change height. The main walkway runs past vendors and up into the market.

environment-2.firstReading: A hillside market follows curved stone stairs and landings down to partly awash vendor platforms.
environment-2.note: The nested levels keep upper landings available as water covers the lower edges. Connected steps link the foreground to the upper market.

environment-2.firstReading: A boardwalk follows the shore beside roofed market platforms held over the water on overhead pulley rigs.
environment-2.note: Lines descend from the beams and drums to the decks, which can plausibly change height. The shore-side boardwalk and stairs stay continuous.

environment-2.firstReading: A stepped boardwalk passes a low vendor platform buoyed by pale floats inside tall uprights and another raised platform farther out.
environment-2.note: The visible floats supply the clearest mechanism, with taller frames also suggesting vertical movement. The public route continues up the boardwalk from the foreground.

environment-2.firstReading: A narrow timber walkway crosses the harbor market beside a large diagonal boom reaching toward a canopy stall.
environment-2.note: The walkway and stalls are clear. The boom looks articulated, but what it moves and how that responds to changing water level stay ambiguous.
